title: Saviour, Cast a Pitying Eye
description: Saviour, Cast a Pitying Eye in Tonic Solfa to SPANISH HYMN, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. His brother John printed them in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 116.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Sevens, six lines (7.7.7.7.7.7), and this page sets them to SPANISH HYMN; any other Sevens, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: Sa-viour, cast a pity-ing eye, Bid my sins and sor-rows end; Whith-er should a sin-ner fly? Art not thou the sin-ner's friend? Rest in thee I gasp to find, Wret-ched I, and poor, and blind.

lines: Saviour, cast a pitying eye,
Bid my sins and sorrows end;
Whither should a sinner fly?
Art not thou the sinner's friend?
Rest in thee I gasp to find,
Wretched I, and poor, and blind.
Haste, O haste, to my relief!
From the iron furnace take;
Bid me of my sin and grief,
For thy love and mercy's sake;
Set my heart at liberty,
Show forth all thy power in me.
Me, the vilest of the race,
Most unholy, most unclean;
Me, the farthest from thy face,
Full of misery and sin;
Me with arms of love receive,
Me, of sinners chief, forgive!
Jesus, on thine only name
For salvation I depend,
In thy gracious hands I am,
Save me, save me to the end;
Let the utmost grace be given,
Save me quite from hell to heaven.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to SPANISH HYMN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
